sweep.in_sweep_persistence_stamp: 5/18 sectors - fails persistence - blend-suspect (HIT line also flagged: high-contamination - blend risk)

odd_even.verdict_text: The two dips are different sizes — odd transits dip 0.288% but even transits dip 0.143% (50% apart). That is the classic sign of an eclipsing binary whose real period is twice the candidate period.

kill_reason: odd/even alternating eclipse depths at 2P (odd 0.288% vs even 0.143%, ratio 0.50); double-period windows 0.411% / 0.274% at refined 25.9239 d, no ellipsoidal wave (-0.092% @ -3.7 sigma). Eclipsing binary in the aperture; true period ~25.92 d, the sweep's 12.9644 d is the half-period alias.

double_period.verdict_text: The light between the eclipses is flat — quadratures sit at 0.9993 and the shoulders at 1.0002, a difference of -0.092% ± 0.025%, so there is no twin-star ellipsoidal wave. That is consistent with a real planet — or with a binary whose stars are too far apart to distort each other.
double_period.note: Post-gate diagnostic (driver gated at stage b); run to complete the brief's (a)-(c) fold set.

reclassification_note: Fold completion AGREES with and REFINES the in-sweep stamp. The stamp's 'fails persistence - blend-suspect' said the alias-ephemeris signal does not behave like a constant-depth planet train; the folds identify what it actually is - an eclipsing binary with two unequal eclipses. With contratio 0.301 the EB may be the target or a neighbour inside the aperture (folds alone cannot separate those; centroid work could), but the planet reading is dead either way. Verdict class follows the batch precedent for this fold signature (cf. TIC 294671352, contratio 0.272, LIKELY BINARY).
